issues.legal_issue: A representative suit concerning a public charitable or religious trust is not maintainable when permission was granted jointly to several persons, one dies before filing, and the survivors file without obtaining fresh permission.
material_facts: Several persons obtained written permission to institute a suit concerning a public trust.
One of them died before the suit was instituted.
The surviving persons instituted the suit without obtaining fresh permission.
The trial court found the suit maintainable, but the High Court set aside that decision; the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The survivors’ suit was incompetent because the permission was a joint authority to sue. They were required to obtain fresh permission before instituting the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 92(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a suit for the specified reliefs concerning a public charitable or religious trust must conform to the Advocate-General’s written consent. Consent granted to several persons is a joint authority that must be exercised by all of them; if one dies before institution, the survivors cannot sue under that consent and must obtain fresh permission. The Court relied on Muddala Bhagavannarayana v. Vadapalli Perumallacharyulu, Pitchayya v. Venkatakrishnamacharlu, Sibte Rasul v. Sibte Nabi, Venkatesha Malia v. B. Ramaya Hegade, Musammat Ali Begam v. Badr-ul-Islam Ali Khan, and Raja Anand Rao v. Ramdas Daduram, and declined to follow Sheo Ram v. Rama Chand. The Court distinguished death after valid institution, which does not render the suit incompetent.

rule.if: public_trust_representative_suit and joint_permission_to_multiple_people and authorized_person_died_before_filing and survivors_filed_without_fresh_permission

predicates.public_trust_representative_suit: The claimants instituted a representative suit seeking relief concerning a public charitable or religious trust.
predicates.joint_permission_to_multiple_people: The relevant authority granted permission to several people jointly to institute the suit.
predicates.authorized_person_died_before_filing: One of the people to whom permission was granted died before the suit was instituted.
predicates.survivors_filed_without_fresh_permission: The remaining people instituted the suit without obtaining new permission after that death.

issues.definition: When claimants bring a representative trust suit under joint permission, an authorized person dies before filing, and the survivors proceed without fresh permission, the suit is not maintainable.
